description: Threat anticipation can justify surveillance emergency power and weak democratic oversight.
Technology deployment can outrun review audit and rights protection.
Preparedness systems can decay between crises when attention and funding fade.
Prevention and maintenance can be delayed because benefits are less visible than crisis response.
Participation becomes fragile when public voice does not change decisions or budgets.
Signals can be detected but ignored if institutions lack receptivity or authority.
Pilots and sandboxes can shift risk onto vulnerable groups without safeguards.
Scanning and scenarios fail when not connected to authority finance or delivery.
